evidence.finding: Logged-in agents fell from 49 before the incident to 44 at 09:15 and as low as 33; the post-incident mean declined 26.72%.
Productive staffing decreased 25.58%, from a pre-incident mean of 45.2 agents to 33.64 afterward.
Scheduled staffing remained fixed at 49 while the scheduled-to-logged gap grew from zero to as many as 16 agents.
A center-wide workforce notice reported multiple same-day absences at 09:15, matching the staffing-loss onset.
Mean service level fell from 90.34% before the incident to 66.86% afterward.
Mean ASA increased from 25.21 seconds to 56.66 seconds after incident onset.
All four queues lost approximately 25–29% of staffed capacity and experienced service-level deterioration, demonstrating a center-wide capacity loss rather than localized misallocation.
Offered calls increased 5.97%, adding pressure but not accounting for the much larger capacity and service deterioration.

primary_root_cause_detail: Multiple same-day absences beginning at 09:15 created an unplanned logged-in staffing deficit. Scheduled headcount remained at 49, but logged-in and productive staffing fell sharply, reducing center-wide capacity and degrading service across all queues.
recommended_actions: Activate same-day absence and reserve-staff escalation procedures when scheduled-to-logged gaps emerge.
Configure real-time alerts for material logged-in and productive staffing losses by center and queue.
Rebalance available agents and prioritize critical queues during recovery.
Review absence-notification timing, backup coverage, and workforce contingency thresholds.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Aggregate volume increased only 5.97%, and Billing degraded despite a 13.96% volume decrease.
Center AHT decreased 0.32%, while queue-level AHT changes remained between -0.44% and +0.75%.
Staffing losses and service degradation occurred across every queue, with no material transfer-rate increase or routing event.
No platform event was recorded; the visible event instead identified same-day absences at incident onset.
Mean adherence increased from 92.24% to 93.71%, so adherence decline did not cause the capacity loss.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by center-wide same-day absences beginning at 09:15. Logged-in and productive capacity fell by roughly one-quarter while schedules and adherence remained stable. Moderate volume growth increased pressure but was not the primary cause.
